content: 1. Strontium ranelate reduces the absorption of tetracyclines in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to decreased levels of tetracyclines. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. To avoid chelation with magnesium, administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after each dose. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. Strontium ranelate should be suspended during antibiotic therapy. 2. Tetracyclines enhance the effects of succinylcholine through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 3. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose as per dosage modification guidelines. 4. Tetracyclines reduce the effects of temocillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 5. Bismuth subsalicylate decreases the absorption of tetracyclines in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to reduced levels of tetracyclines. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 6. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 7. Tetracyclines and tretinoin (oral or topical) exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of phototoxicity. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 8. Tripotassium dicitrato bismuthate reduces the absorption of tetracyclines in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to decreased levels of tetracyclines. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 9. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of tetracyclines by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with CYP3A substrates, as even minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate according to product labeling. 10. Tetracyclines reduce the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 11. Metronidazole reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 12. Tetracyclines enhance the effects of vecuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 13. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for signs of venetoclax toxicities. 14. Bismuth subsalicylate enhances the anticoagulant effects of warfarin. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 15. Tetracyclines increase the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor. 17. Bismuth subsalicylate and acebutolol exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially causing severe hypertension due to renal prostaglandin synthesis blockade. Use caution and monitor. 18. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Bismuth subsalicylate and atenolol exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially causing severe hypertension due to renal prostaglandin synthesis blockade. Use caution and monitor. 20. Tetracyclines increase the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Metronidazole increases the toxicity of amifampridine, which can cause seizures. Coadministration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may increase this risk. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Tetracyclines increase the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce avanafil clearance, increasing systemic exposure and associated adverse events. The maximum recommended dose of avanafil is 50 mg, not to exceed once every 24 hours for patients taking concomitant moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 29. Tetracyclines reduce the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 30. Metronidazole reduces the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 31. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Bismuth subsalicylate reduces the effects of benazepril through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Salicylates may also increase the nephrotoxic effects of ACE inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 33. Bismuth subsalicylate and betaxolol exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially causing severe hypertension due to renal prostaglandin synthesis blockade. Use caution and monitor. 34. Bismuth subsalicylate and bisoprolol exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially causing severe hypertension due to renal prostaglandin synthesis blockade. Use caution and monitor. 35. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 36. Bosentan reduces the levels or effects of tetracyclines by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 37. Tetracyclines increase the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor. 39. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Tetracyclines increase the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implants by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor patients already on buprenorphine subdermal implants who require newly initiated treatment with CYP3A4 inhibitors for signs and symptoms of overmedication. If the dose of the concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should then be treated with a buprenorphine dosage form that permits dose adjustments. If a CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued in a patient stabilized on buprenorphine, monitor the patient for withdrawal. 41. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implants by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor patients already on buprenorphine subdermal implants who require newly initiated treatment with CYP3A4 inhibitors for signs and symptoms of overmedication. If the dose of the concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should then be treated with a buprenorphine dosage form that permits dose adjustments. If a CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued in a patient stabilized on buprenorphine, monitor the patient for withdrawal. 42. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine long-acting injection by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Patients who transfer to buprenorphine long-acting injection from transmucosal buprenorphine coadministered with CYP3A4 inhibitors should be monitored to ensure buprenorphine plasma levels are adequate. Within 2 weeks, if signs and symptoms of buprenorphine toxicity or overdose occur and the concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, transition the patient back to a buprenorphine formulation that permits dose adjustments. 43. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Tetracyclines increase the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Exercise caution with concomitant use of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 45. Tetracyclines increase the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 47. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 48. Tetracyclines increase the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 49. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the capivasertib dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 50. Tetracyclines increase the levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Bismuth subsalicylate and carvedilol exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially causing severe hypertension due to renal prostaglandin synthesis blockade. Use caution and monitor. 53. Tetracyclines reduce the effects of cefdinir through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor. 54. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of carvedilol by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 55. Tetracyclines reduce the effects of cefditoren through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor. 56. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of tetracyclines by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Increase the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 62. Cholestyramine reduces the levels of metronidazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 63. Cholestyramine reduces the levels of tetracyclines by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 64. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 65. Tetracyclines reduce the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 66. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 67. Metronidazole reduces the levels or effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Inhibition of CYP3A4 will reduce clopidogrel bioactivation. 68. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of clozapine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
